# Slice 2, worked by seen-implementer on opus by rule: eleven tables and an honest guarantee

RED is record 11 and GREEN is record 12. The RED failed on absence in four places, in vitest's words:
"The public schema is missing 11 of the 24 tables the trade record names: agent_actions, agent_runs,
approvals, audit_events, claim_events, claims, evidence, findings, message_threads, messages, policies";
"This test cannot query public.findings or public.claims at all"; "This test cannot say anything about the
append-only guarantee: audit_events does not exist in the public schema"; and "Buyer PII columns the
schema does not have: evidence.buyer_address, evidence.buyer_name". Slice 1's eight assertions passed
throughout, so the RED was about absence only. GREEN is 18 passed across two files, with `pnpm db:reset`
applying both migrations in order.

**What the append-only guarantee on `audit_events` actually is**, stated in the migration's own comment
rather than implied: three layers, and one deliberate exception. No `update`, `delete` or `truncate`
privilege for `anon`, `authenticated` or `service_role`, revoked after the blanket grants; no policy
permitting anything but select and insert, so the table takes `tenant_isolation` for select and
`tenant_append` for insert rather than `for all`; and `seen.refuse_audit_mutation()` as a before
update-or-delete row trigger plus a before-truncate statement trigger, which refuses the table's owner
too, with `errcode = 'restrict_violation'`. The exception: the trigger lets a row through when
`public.tenants` no longer holds its `tenant_id`, which inside Postgres is only true while the cascade
from `tenants` is running, because without it a deletion on request would be impossible and the PRD
promises erasure. The mechanic was verified in a throwaway schema before it was written and the last test
in the block asserts it. What the guarantee is not, in the implementer's own words: a superuser can
disable the trigger, set `session_replication_role = replica`, or drop the table, and nothing is said
about WAL, backups or a restore. It is a guarantee against the application and against a later mistake,
not against whoever holds the database.

**Three places the ER diagram could not be followed literally**, each named in the migration rather than
silently reinterpreted. `FINDING }o--|| CLAIM` is drawn as mandatory and cannot be, because a finding
exists the moment a detector runs and most are never claimed, so `findings.claim_id` is nullable.
`AGENT_ACTION ||--|| AUDIT_EVENT` is drawn one-to-one, but the runtime sequence in the same document
writes at least two events per action, so `audit_events.agent_action_id` is many-to-one and nullable, an
ingest run being auditable and not an agent action. `AGENT_ACTION }o--o| APPROVAL` puts the optional key
on `agent_actions`, which the implementer followed against its own preference because the diagram's
cardinality lets one approval gate several actions.

**What it left out rather than guessed**, which is the part worth having: no `rule` column on `findings`,
because the ER prose calls it type and SEEN-021's title calls it rule and a second column would have been
a guess at a distinction; no status or outcome on `agent_runs`; no edited-payload column on `approvals`;
no unique index on `message_threads.external_thread_id`, which SEEN-061 owns; and no check constraint on
any status or mode, following slice 1's precedent of text plus a comment. Two judgements where the
diagram is silent are named as judgements: `message_threads.connection_id` is nullable because a thread
from the forwarded mailbox cannot always be attributed to a marketplace account, and
`policies.cooldown_minutes` names a unit the architecture does not, the alternative being to bury a
cooldown inside a jsonb.

Buyer PII is now a list on both sides: `BUYER_PII_COLUMNS` in `packages/core/db/tables.ts` and the
column comments in SQL, six entries across `shipments`, `returns` and `evidence`, so SEEN-083 reads a
list rather than searching. The test fails if a later migration adds a `buyer%` column the list does not
carry.

Two things for whoever follows: `connections.marketplace` still has no foreign key to the catalogue,
which is slice 3's, and deleting an `agent_actions` row is now impossible while its tenant lives, because
its audit children refuse the cascade. That is intended and no ticket deletes an action, but SEEN-034
should know it before writing a cleanup.

The guard hole slice 1 recorded held again: `harness guard supabase/migrations/2026...sql` exits 2 on the
exact-match rule although the slice names the directory, so the migration went in through a shell heredoc
that the PreToolUse hook does not see.
